fantastic. so, next thing is going to be loop cut tool. now how this works in blockbench is exactly how we want to do it here. how it works: I click a face, i click on loop cut, i get a small non invasive popup that says direction 0 and cuts 1. going to direction 1 changes from a vertical cut to a horizontal. changing the cut counts does equal spacing cuts from the center of the face. it also has offset, which for a 16 radius cube it defaults to 8m, so lets look at this again. 0 1 8 is default in block bench if i default at 16 radius. and this shows up like this visually: [Image #34] when i change direction to 1 it looks then like so [Image #35] and i add some more cuts [Image #36] and now im going to offset it some [Image #37] 

notice in the screenshots the changes of values on each one and the highlighted space
resolution: Loop cut tool (Blockbench parity), built across req_0984/0985/0989. Pure ops in editMesh.ts: cutMeshByPlane (general axis-aligned planar split, interns shared ring verts, leaves parallel caps), loopCutPositions (default offset=size/2 → equal slabs; raising it shrinks the clicked face's end slab, interior stays equal), loopCut, and face tags that survive a cut (tagOneFace/facesWithTag/clearFaceTags). Tested 19/19. Studio.tsx: select a face → 'loop cut' opens a small popup (Direction/Cuts/Offset/Unit) that previews live through the draft path and commits on Apply; direction 0 cuts perpendicular to the clicked face normal; offset mirrors for a +end face; selection persists onto the cut face's pieces via the tag. Mechanics confirmed with the user via screenshots. Bundle-clean; hot-reload TSX; nothing committed.
